criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: Verified manually with headless Chrome (Puppeteer): all 9 tabs reachable, every card/row drills down one level, Sample/Real toggle correctly labels fictional data, stale-data warning fires on the current 7-day-21-hour-old manifest, and deleting a story from plan.json and reloading removes it from the page (confirmed no hard-coded values). No automated test suite added for this static page — session CC-20260924-x7q3.

criteria.text: Given a Basecamp comment with '##Critique##', When the system processes the comment, Then a review item is created with status 'Pending'.
Given a comment with '## Review ##', When the system processes the comment, Then no review item is created.
Trust: The system logs the detection event with the exact comment ID.

stories.notes: All 3 criteria verified by tests (review_queue/test_intake.py, test_intake_routes.py, test_logging_config.py) and a live uvicorn+curl run. Comments come via a CommentSource interface with fixtures/HTTP; the live SQL Server reader for Basecamp_MessageBoards_MessageComments is deferred (needs credentials + driver). Review Queue is in-memory until a database is chosen.

criteria.text: Given a Basecamp project with submissions, when the system retrieves data, then it includes comments, attachments, and links.
Given a Basecamp project with no submissions, when the system attempts to retrieve data, then it returns an empty dataset.
Trust: The system logs all data retrieval actions with timestamps and user IDs.

stories.notes: All 3 criteria verified by tests against simulated Basecamp API responses (test_submission_retrieval.py: AC1 comments/attachments/links, AC2 empty dataset, trust audit log with timestamp + requested_by_user_id on success, failure and unexpected errors) and by retrieve_submissions.py --demo. NOT yet run against live Basecamp: no OAuth app is registered, and Basecamp offers no API keys. Failure paths tested: 429 (Retry-After, capped), invalid token (401/403, no retry), network failure/5xx (3 attempts). Retrieved comments feed STORY-001 intake unchanged (test_submission_comment_source.py); SQL and API comment ids are the same Basecamp recording ids.

criteria.text: Given a submission is processed, when an action is taken, then it is logged in the audit trail.
Given a submission is processed without human review, when the system attempts to auto-approve, then it blocks the action.
Trust: The system ensures no credentials are stored in source code or shared documents.
criteria.evidence: backend/src/services/guardrails/credentialLeakGuardrail.js (assertNoCredentialLeaks) + credentialLeakGuardrail.test.js (12/12 passing) + backend/src/scripts/scanForCredentials.js (npm run scan:secrets exits 0 against the repo)

stories.notes: Criteria 2 and 3 genuinely pass and are covered by unit tests (npm test, 30/30 passing repo-wide) plus a real repo-wide scan (npm run scan:secrets, exit 0). Criterion 1 (audit trail logging) is not yet built — it needs the database layer, which does not exist yet per Master Spec §27, and is left false rather than ticked prematurely.

outstanding: Given a submission is processed, when an action is taken, then it is logged in the audit trail.

criteria.text: Given historical critique and feedback comments for a Stress Test are indexed in a vector database stored outside SQL Server, when a new submission for that Stress Test is reviewed, then the system returns the top 5–10 most similar cases from that same Stress Test only.
Given a submission for one Stress Test, when historical cases are retrieved, then no case from a different Stress Test is returned.
Given the vector database or the embedding service is unavailable, when retrieval runs, then the review continues without historical examples and the error is shown to the reviewer.
Given no similar historical cases exist, when retrieval runs, then the system returns an empty list and says so, rather than failing.
Trust: Historical examples never override the current Stress Test rules, and existing SQL Server tables and procedures are never changed.
